drop.title: Water Finds the Cheapest Crack, and the Threshold Finds Itself

title: Water Finds the
Cheapest Crack
slides.dek: Give every pore a random toughness and let a fluid break only the weakest pore on its wet frontier, forever. The path it carves is the cheapest crossing there is, and it finds the critical threshold with no dial set.

slides.body: A fluid with no map does the only thing it can: at every step it breaks the *weakest pore* on its wet frontier and floods it. Run it until a finger touches the far side and trace the wet route back. That route is not just *a* way across, it is the one that *minimises the toughest pore* you are forced to push through. That is the classic *minimax*, or bottleneck-shortest, path, and the greedy weakest-frontier rule is exactly how you solve it. It is Prim's 1957 step for a minimum spanning tree, wearing a fluid's costume. To be sure, the build computed the invasion's bottleneck and an independent Kruskal crossing on *160 of 160* random rocks. They agreed every time.

Nowhere in the rule is there a density or a critical value, yet the fluid finds one. Tally the toughness of *every* pore it accepts over a long run: dead flat up to about 0.59, then a cliff. It almost never accepts a pore tougher than *0.5927*, and that is no accident, it is the *percolation threshold* of the square lattice. Only a tenth of one percent of accepted pores clear it. Run the crossing on rocks of growing size instead, and the average bottleneck climbs from below onto that same 0.5927. Two different questions, one constant, and nobody told it the answer. This is *self-organised criticality*, Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld, 1987.

lines.sub: rotate format back to app after research #055, and reopen the percolation lattice vein idle since #048. picked invasion percolation (wilkinson & willemsen, 1983): the greedy, moving cousin of the static percolation picture from #039

three live modules over one binary min-heap driving weakest-frontier-first invasion: the fractal crossing and its ringed bottleneck, a center-out self-organised-criticality histogram, and a live minimax-equals-bottleneck convergence

checked offline first, mulberry32-seeded so ssr equals client: invasion bottleneck is byte-identical to an independent kruskal minimax value on 160/160 fields; mean crossing bottleneck climbs 0.5887 -> 0.5932 onto p_c = 0.5927 as the rock grows

slides.big:
one greedy rule.
the *cheapest crack*
and the *threshold.*
slides.sub: Watch the wet region grow fractal until a finger breaks through at pore 1,293 of 3,136, then the least-resistance route lights up, ringed at its single hardest pore, bottleneck 0.6062. A center-out run parks its accepted toughness against p_c with only 0.1% above it, and a live convergence climbs 0.5728, 0.5885, 0.5928 onto the threshold. A fluid running a shortest-path algorithm, and discovering a critical constant, at once.
